Linear Model fit with lm.rrpp

Number of observations: 40
Number of dependent variables: 24  
Data space dimensions: 24

Number of permutations: 1000

    data = pleth.gdf, print.progress = FALSE)

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] procD.lm function
parts:
Erika,

 

You should use the vignettes and help files that are provided within geomorph, not the guide (which is no longer maintained).

 

For some time, Geomorph, and RRPP, follow more standard S-3 programming in R, and mirror what is generated by base-R functions such as ‘lm’. Thus, one fits the model, and results are received such as you saw. Then, one must request ‘anova’, ‘summary’ or some other aspect of that fit to receive summary statistics, anova tables and the like.

 

Please see the vignettes and help files of current versions of geomorph. They provide extensive example for proper use of the package.

 

Dean

model1<-procD.lm(coords ~ site + logcs, data = gdf1, iter = 999, RRPP = FALSE, print.progress = T)

anova(model1)

 

y<-two.d.array(myGPA$coords)

y

model2<-procD.lm(y~gdf1$site+gdf1$logcs,iter=99)

anova(model2)

 

model3<-procD.lm(myGPA$coords~myGPA$site+log(myGPA$Csize))

anova(model3)

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] procD.lm function
parts:
You have different significance levels across models because you requested a different type of permutation in model 1 relative to models 2 & 3. For model1 you stated RRPP = FALSE, but left this blank in model2 and model3.  Since the default is ‘TRUE, that makes a difference.


Note also that the rest of the statistical results: SS, MS, R2 and F values are identical across the 3 models; as they should be.  Only Z and P differ in your model1, as these are affected by the permutation distribution. 

 

Again I recommend a careful reading of all help files and vignettes to learn and understand the many options for each function in geomorph.


Best,

Dean

Mike

As a bit of an experiment, I installed geomorph from github without building vignettes (note that build_vignettes = FALSE is the default option).  I got the same error with vignette("geomorph.PCA").  Then I installed again, changing build_vignettes = TRUE and vignette("geomorph.PCA”) worked.

Note that I discovered some issues I could not explain when trying to install from github.  I updated R from 4.0.0 to 4.0.2 and made sure all of my packages were up to date, which seemed to fix some inexplicable errors.  It seems R had some rapid updates from 4.0.0 to 4.0.2 and there have been a lot of bug fixes noted on CRAN.  I’m not saying this could be a problem for issues with vignettes, but a combination of updating and making sure to build vignettes upon installation worked for me.

Mike
On Jul 20, 2020, at 12:30 PM, Crispo, Erika <ecr...@pace.edu> wrote:

I am able to view the vignettes for assistance, functions, and digitize3D, but vignette("geomorph.PCA") gives me a warning that the vignette is not found.
 
 
From: geomorph-...@googlegroups.com [mailto:geomorph-...@googlegroups.com]On Behalf Of Mike Collyer
Sent: Monday, July 20, 2020 12:23 PM
To: geomorph R package <geomorph-...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] procD.lm function
 
Why are you trying to knit Rmd files?  Vignettes should install automatically when installing a package from CRAN, and are an option when using devtools::install_github, using the argument build_vignettes = TRUE.  There could be myriad reasons why knitting an Rmd file does not work, that are not due to a programming error (might be a dependency error) but users should never have to knit Rmd files for a package in order to have vignettes.
 
Mike
